note: WAEC English Paper 1 (Lexis & Structure) round 1: 80 lexis + 80 structure items in WASSCE style.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The chairman was OVERJOYED when the results were announced. A word closest in meaning to OVERJOYED is
questions.explanation: Overjoyed means extremely happy; thrilled is the nearest in meaning, while upset is almost the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The clerk was noted for being METICULOUS in his work. METICULOUS means
questions.explanation: Meticulous describes someone who pays great attention to detail and is careful and precise.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Supplies of food became SCARCE after the flood. SCARCE is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Scarce means not enough to meet the need; hard to find captures that meaning.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The crowd's reaction to the news was HOSTILE. A word nearest in meaning to HOSTILE is
questions.explanation: Hostile means showing opposition or unfriendliness; excited, curious and silent do not fit.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Despite the injuries, the athlete was RESILIENT and returned to play. RESILIENT means
questions.explanation: Resilient describes the ability to recover quickly from difficulty or injury.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: His FRUGAL habits allowed him to save for his children's fees. FRUGAL is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Frugal means using money or resources carefully, the same as thrifty; wasteful is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The DILIGENT student always finished her assignments early. DILIGENT means
questions.explanation: Diligent means showing steady, careful effort in one's work — hardworking.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The sky turned OMINOUS before the storm broke. OMINOUS is nearest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Ominous means giving the impression that something bad is going to happen — threatening.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The minister was CANDID about the challenges facing the economy. CANDID means
questions.explanation: Candid means frank, honest and direct in saying what one thinks.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The old bridge was ROBUST enough to carry heavy vehicles. ROBUST means
questions.explanation: Robust describes something strong and sturdy, built to withstand heavy use.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The lecture was so TEDIOUS that half the students dozed off. TEDIOUS means
questions.explanation: Tedious means slow, long and dull — boring; the students' dozing confirms it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She was AVERSE to speaking in public. AVERSE is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: Averse means strongly opposed or unwilling to do something.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The beauty of the sunset was EPHEMERAL; it lasted only a few minutes. EPHEMERAL means
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time — short-lived.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager offered a COMPROMISE solution that satisfied both parties. COMPROMISE means
questions.explanation: A compromise is a solution where each side gives up something — a middle-ground result.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The store was ABUNDANT with fresh produce. A word opposite in meaning to ABUNDANT is
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities; scarce (not enough) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The judge was known to be BENEVOLENT towards first-time offenders. A word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT is
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind and generous; cruel is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The soldier was COURAGEOUS when he entered the burning building. A word opposite in meaning to COURAGEOUS is
questions.explanation: Courageous means brave and not afraid; timid (shy, easily frightened) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The classroom was CHAOTIC during the fire drill. A word opposite in meaning to CHAOTIC is
questions.explanation: Chaotic means in complete disorder; orderly is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Her family was GENEROUS with food for the visitors. A word opposite in meaning to GENEROUS is
questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give freely; selfish (unwilling to share) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He was very HUMBLE about his success. A word opposite in meaning to HUMBLE is
questions.explanation: Humble means having a modest view of oneself; arrogant (excessively proud) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The teacher was LENIENT about late submissions. A word opposite in meaning to LENIENT is
questions.explanation: Lenient means not strict or severe; strict is the direct opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: His house was MODEST in size but full of love. A word opposite in meaning to MODEST is
questions.explanation: Modest here means not large or showy; grand (large and impressive) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager was RIGID in his decision. A word opposite in meaning to RIGID is
questions.explanation: Rigid means not able to change or bend; flexible is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The school has always been TOLERANT of different customs. A word opposite in meaning to TOLERANT is
questions.explanation: Tolerant means accepting of other views and customs; intolerant refuses them.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The market was TRANSIENT during the festival, closing after a few days. A word opposite in meaning to TRANSIENT is
questions.explanation: Transient means lasting only a short time; permanent (fixed, lasting) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The hospital corridor was VACANT when the nurses took their break. A word opposite in meaning to VACANT is
questions.explanation: Vacant means empty, not occupied; occupied is the direct opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Her apology was SINCERE and everyone forgave her. A word opposite in meaning to SINCERE is
questions.explanation: Sincere means genuine and meant in good faith; fake (not genuine) is the opposite.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The old man's eyes were RHEUMY after the funeral. RHEUMY here means
questions.explanation: Rheumy means filled with tears or mucus; watery fits a man who has been crying.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The student's excuses were BIZARRE and nobody believed them. BIZARRE here means
questions.explanation: Bizarre means very strange or unusual; nobody would believe strange excuses.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The road to the village was so BUMPY that our luggage fell out of the car. BUMPY here means
questions.explanation: A bumpy road has many raised lumps or holes that shake a vehicle.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The company LAY OFF many workers when orders fell. LAY OFF here means
questions.explanation: To lay off workers means to dismiss them from work, usually for economic reasons.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The boy's behaviour was OUTRAGEOUS at the party. OUTRAGEOUS means
questions.explanation: Outrageous means shocking or far beyond what is acceptable — shockingly bad.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: If we wanted to keep our seats we had to PAY UP. PAY UP means
questions.explanation: Pay up means to pay the full amount that is owed, usually at once.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: His voice was TORN between joy and fear. TORN here means
questions.explanation: Torn between two feelings means divided by them, not sure which dominates.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The two brothers FELL OUT over the family land. FELL OUT means
questions.explanation: To fall out with someone means to have a quarrel and stop being friendly.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new policy is set to TAKE EFFECT from January. TAKE EFFECT means
questions.explanation: When a policy takes effect it formally begins to operate and apply.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The student was SUSPENDED from school for fighting. SUSPENDED here means
questions.explanation: Suspension in school means being temporarily removed from classes as a punishment.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The farmer's harvest was BOUNTIFUL this season. BOUNTIFUL means
questions.explanation: Bountiful means abundant; a bountiful harvest is a very large one.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The child was SPOILED by too much attention from the grandparents. SPOILED here means
questions.explanation: A spoiled child is one who has been pampered and given too much, so he behaves badly.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The politician's promises were VACUOUS and meant nothing. VACUOUS means
questions.explanation: Vacuous means empty of real meaning or substance; the promises meant nothing.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The team's performance was PATHETIC in the final match. PATHETIC means
questions.explanation: Pathetic here means disappointingly poor or deserving of pity.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Her explanation was CIRCUMLOCUTORY and wasted a lot of time. CIRCUMLOCUTORY means
questions.explanation: Circumlocutory means using more words than necessary in an indirect way — long-winded.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The news came as a SHOCK: the school was to close. SHOCK in this sentence means
questions.explanation: As a noun here, shock means a sudden unpleasant surprise that stuns people.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When asked about the plan, the clerk accidentally LET THE CAT OUT OF THE BAG. The expression means he
questions.explanation: To let the cat out of the bag means to reveal a secret, usually by mistake.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: That new phone COSTS AN ARM AND A LEG. The expression means it is
questions.explanation: To cost an arm and a leg is a common idiom for being very expensive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You HIT THE NAIL ON THE HEAD when you said the problem was money. The expression means you
questions.explanation: To hit the nail on the head means to describe exactly what is causing a situation.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We meet only ONCE IN A BLUE MOON. The expression means we meet
questions.explanation: Once in a blue moon describes something that happens very rarely.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I don't want to join the match; I'm UNDER THE WEATHER. The expression means I am
questions.explanation: To be under the weather is an idiom for feeling slightly unwell or sick.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The lawyer submitted the papers AT THE ELEVENTH HOUR. The expression means
questions.explanation: At the eleventh hour means at the very last possible moment, just before it is too late.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Failing the first test turned out to be A BLESSING IN DISGUISE. The expression means it
questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is something that seems bad at first but later produces good results.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: My sister SPILLED THE BEANS about our surprise party. The expression means she
questions.explanation: To spill the beans means to tell a secret or reveal information that should be kept.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The test was A PIECE OF CAKE for the class topper. The expression means it was
questions.explanation: A piece of cake is an idiom meaning something very easy to do.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new teacher BROKE THE ICE with a joke at the first lesson. The expression means she
questions.explanation: To break the ice means to ease tension and start a friendly conversation.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He is BARKING UP THE WRONG TREE if he thinks I did it. The expression means he
questions.explanation: Barking up the wrong tree means to pursue a mistaken line of thought or accusation.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The family stayed together THROUGH THICK AND THIN. The expression means
questions.explanation: Through thick and thin means in all circumstances, both good and bad.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: After the crash, the old car was DEAD AS A DOORNAIL. The expression means it was
questions.explanation: Dead as a doornail means completely dead or, for an object, totally useless.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She PUT HER FOOT IN IT when she insulted the guest. The expression means she
questions.explanation: To put one's foot in it means to say or do something tactless and embarrassing.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The two farmers are IN THE SAME BOAT during this election. The expression means they
questions.explanation: In the same boat means in the same difficult situation, with the same risks.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The government has decided to ____ the price of fuel.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is to raise a price (or to increase it); lift and bring do not take 'price'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Students must ____ their projects by Friday.
questions.explanation: We submit an assignment, project or application; the other verbs do not collocate with 'projects' here.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The police want to ____ the man who stole the car.
questions.explanation: The police arrest a criminal; they may fine or warn minor offenders, but arrest fits a thief.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The board ____ a new manager to run the sales department.
questions.explanation: A company appoints someone to a job or position; made, did and took do not collocate here.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The school ____ the inter-house sports this year.
questions.explanation: We organize an event such as a sports competition; the other verbs are not used with events.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The government will ____ measures to reduce traffic.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is to take measures (or to take action) to deal with a problem.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The company ____ a lot of money on advertising.
questions.explanation: You spend money on something; 'paid' needs a person as object (paid the workers).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The hall must stay clean; don't ____ a mess.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is to make a mess; we do not 'do', 'have' or 'take' a mess.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The judge ____ the man to ten years in prison.
questions.explanation: A judge sentences a prisoner to a term; 'sentenced to ten years' is the legal collocation.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The students ____ the visit to the museum.
questions.explanation: We enjoy a visit, trip or game; the other verbs do not collocate with 'the visit'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The firemen ____ the fire before it spread to the next building.
questions.explanation: To put out a fire means to make it stop burning; the other phrasal verbs mean different things.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You will ____ a lot from this lesson.
questions.explanation: The formal collocation is to benefit from something; 'benefit a lot' fits best here.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The team ____ the final match 3–1.
questions.explanation: You win a match or game; 'beat' is used with a person or team (beat the rivals).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The news ____ quickly, and the whole village came out.
questions.explanation: News spreads from person to person; it does not grow, run or walk.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She always ____ good care of her younger brother.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is to take care of someone; we also say 'look after', not 'make care'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The bank will not ____ a loan to anyone without security.
questions.explanation: A bank grants (or gives) a loan; it does not sell, make or buy one for a customer.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The law ____ everyone to pay taxes.
questions.explanation: The law requires or obliges people to do something; suggests, hopes and dreams are too weak.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The singer ____ a new song for the festival.
questions.explanation: Artists release a song or album to the public; the other verbs do not fit.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The thief ____ the window to enter the house.
questions.explanation: The thief broke the window; 'break' is the verb used with glass in this context.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You should ____ your hands before eating.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is to wash your hands before eating; the other verbs do not fit.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The doctor ____ the patient to rest for a week.
questions.explanation: The doctor advised the patient to rest; 'suggest' cannot take 'person + to-infinitive' like this.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: WAEC is an ____ examination taken at the end of secondary school.
questions.explanation: WAEC is an external examination (set by an outside body); school-set tests are internal.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By the time the police arrived, the thieves ____.
questions.explanation: The fleeing happened before the police arrived in the past, so the past perfect 'had fled' is required.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She has lived in this house ____ 2015.
questions.explanation: Since is used with a point in time (2015); for is used with a period (eight years).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: They ____ English for three years now.
questions.explanation: An action that started in the past and continues 'now' takes the present perfect: have studied.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: While I ____ home, I met an old friend.
questions.explanation: A longer background action in the past is put in the past continuous: was walking.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The train ____ at six o'clock tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: Timetabled future events use the simple present: the train leaves at six o'clock.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: If it rains, we ____ the match.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional, the if-clause is present and the main clause takes will + verb: will cancel.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He ____ his keys, so he could not open the door.
questions.explanation: Losing the keys happened before he failed to open the door, so the past perfect is used: had lost.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Look! The baby ____.
questions.explanation: 'Look!' shows the action is happening now, so the present continuous is needed: is sleeping.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By next week, we ____ the results.
questions.explanation: An action completed before a future point uses the future perfect: will have received.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When I was a child, I ____ my grandmother every weekend.
questions.explanation: A repeated past habit uses the simple past: visited.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The books ____ by the teacher yesterday.
questions.explanation: A finished passive action at a past time uses was/were + past participle: were checked.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: This is the best film I ____ this year.
questions.explanation: A period that is still open ('this year') takes the present perfect: have seen.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He ____ in Lagos until 2020, then moved to Abuja.
questions.explanation: A completed past period before another past event uses the simple past: lived.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The bridge was damaged last month; it ____ since then.
questions.explanation: 'Since then' links a past event to now, so the present perfect passive is used: has been repaired.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Neither the students nor the teacher ____ present.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'teacher' (singular): was.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Each of the boys ____ a book.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' is always singular, so the verb takes the singular form: has.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The number of students in the class ____ this term.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' is singular (the number itself increased); 'a number of' would be plural.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A number of teachers ____ at the meeting.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb: were.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Each of the girls ____ given a gift.
questions.explanation: 'Each of the girls' is singular, so the correct verb is the singular 'was'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Mathematics ____ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Subjects of study such as mathematics are treated as singular: is.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The news ____ true.
questions.explanation: 'News' ends in -s but is singular in English: the news is true.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The furniture in the room ____ old.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb: is.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: There ____ a book and two pens on the table.
questions.explanation: With 'there is/are' and a list, the verb agrees with the nearest item: a book, so 'is'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The herd of cattle ____ grazing in the field.
questions.explanation: The collective noun 'herd' acts as one unit here, so the singular verb 'is' is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Every student and teacher ____ invited to the ceremony.
questions.explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' after 'every' are treated as one: every student and teacher was.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The rest of the money ____ gone.
questions.explanation: 'Money' is uncountable, so 'the rest of the money' takes the singular verb: has gone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He was accused ____ stealing money.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition is 'accused of' + noun/gerund; 'charged with' is a different pattern.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She is very interested ____ learning French.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'interested in' + noun/gerund.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The success of the project depends ____ everyone's effort.
questions.explanation: The verb 'depend' always takes the preposition 'on': depends on everyone's effort.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He is very good ____ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The collocation is 'good at' + subject/skill (also 'bad at').

questions.subject: English
questions.q: As a child, she was afraid ____ the dark.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'afraid of' + noun.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: They got married ____ 2019.
questions.explanation: We use 'in' with years, months and seasons: married in 2019.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He is proud ____ his son's achievement.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'proud of' + noun.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager is responsible ____ the new office.
questions.explanation: The collocation is 'responsible for' + noun or gerund.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Despite the rain, he insisted ____ playing.
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' takes 'on': insisted on playing.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: All students must participate ____ the exercise.
questions.explanation: The verb 'participate' always takes 'in': participate in the exercise.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She is capable ____ doing the work alone.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'capable' is followed by 'of' + gerund: capable of doing.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Your answer is different ____ mine.
questions.explanation: In formal English, 'different' is followed by 'from': different from mine.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ he was tired, he finished the work.
questions.explanation: Although introduces a contrast (tired, yet finished); because would give the wrong logic.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She studied hard, ____ she passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Passing is the result of studying hard, so the result linker 'so' is needed.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The two brothers have different views; one supports the plan, ____ opposes it.
questions.explanation: With exactly two people, we use 'one ... the other'; 'another' means an additional one.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We left early ____ we could avoid the traffic.
questions.explanation: 'So that' + could expresses purpose: we left early in order to avoid traffic.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He bought a new car ____ his salary was low.
questions.explanation: The contrast (bought a car despite a low salary) needs the concession linker 'even though'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You can have tea ____ coffee.
questions.explanation: When choosing between two things, we use 'or': tea or coffee.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ did he come, nor did he call.
questions.explanation: The paired correlative is 'neither ... nor', so the sentence opens with 'Neither'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The examination was cancelled ____ the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Because' needs a clause; before the noun phrase 'the heavy rain' we use 'due to'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She was late ____ she had missed the bus.
questions.explanation: Missing the bus is the reason for being late, so the cause linker 'because' is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Not only ____ the test, but he also topped the class.
questions.explanation: After the negative 'not only' at the start, the auxiliary comes before the subject: did he pass.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We were about to leave ____ it started to rain.
questions.explanation: 'Was/were about to + verb, when ...' describes an interrupted plan: when it started to rain.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ of the two options is correct.
questions.explanation: With two items and a singular verb, 'Neither ... is' is correct; 'none' is for three or more.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ boy standing at the door is my brother.
questions.explanation: A specific boy (the one at the door) is referred to, so the definite article 'the' is needed.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She has ____ apple in her bag.
questions.explanation: 'Apple' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article 'an' is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I lost my wallet; can you lend me ____ to get home?
questions.explanation: With an uncountable noun in a request where a yes answer is hoped for, 'some' is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The books on the table are ____.
questions.explanation: A possessive pronoun that stands alone after 'are' is needed: ours.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ of the students passed the test.
questions.explanation: 'Every' and 'each' take singular verbs; the plural 'passed' matches 'All of the students'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ was at the party, so we all had fun.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is a singular pronoun meaning all the people; 'every' alone cannot stand as subject.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The man ____ car was stolen called the police.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession in a relative clause: the man whose car was stolen.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The girl ____ won the prize is from this school.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of 'won', referring to a person: who.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: They met each other ____ the first day at school.
questions.explanation: We use 'on' with days and dates: on the first day.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ of the twins is a doctor.
questions.explanation: The singular verb 'is' requires the singular subject 'Each'; 'Both ... are' would be plural.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I have two brothers, and ____ of them lives abroad.
questions.explanation: The singular verb 'lives' matches 'each of them'; 'both' and 'all' would take 'live'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The letter was addressed ____ the manager.
questions.explanation: A letter is addressed to a person: addressed to the manager.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: No sooner had he arrived ____ the phone rang.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner ... than' is the fixed pair; 'hardly ... when' is the other pattern.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ does she like music that she plays the piano.
questions.explanation: The 'so ... that' structure expresses degree and result: so does she like music that ...

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He is so kind ____ everyone trusts him.
questions.explanation: 'So + adjective + that' introduces the result: so kind that everyone trusts him.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Hardly ____ the house when it began to rain.
questions.explanation: After 'hardly' at the start, invert with the auxiliary: hardly had I left the house.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the most appropriate sentence.
questions.A: The harder you study, the better you perform.
questions.B: The hard you study, the well you perform.
questions.C: Harder you study, better you perform.
questions.D: The more you study, the best you perform.
questions.explanation: The comparative pair needs 'the + comparative ... the + comparative': the harder ... the better.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She can swim, ____?
questions.explanation: A question tag repeats the auxiliary of the statement with the opposite polarity: can't she.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: They haven't finished, ____?
questions.explanation: The auxiliary 'have' (in its negative form) is repeated with a positive tag: have they.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I have never seen such a beautiful view. The correct tag is
questions.explanation: With the present perfect and the negative word 'never', the tag is positive: have I.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: What surprised me was ____ the test was so easy.
questions.explanation: A noun clause that completes 'was' is introduced by 'that': was that the test was so easy.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the sentence with the correct word order.
questions.A: Rarely have I had such luck.
questions.B: Rarely I have had such luck.
questions.C: Rarely had I have such luck.
questions.D: Rarely I had have such luck.
questions.explanation: A negative adverb at the start triggers inversion: rarely have I had such luck.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: This is ____ film I have ever seen.
questions.explanation: A superlative comparison needs 'the + superlative': the best film.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Her answer was ____ than mine.
questions.explanation: 'Correct' is a flat adjective in standard usage, so its comparative is 'more correct'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: If I ____ you, I would accept the offer.
questions.explanation: The second conditional uses 'if + past subjunctive': if I were you, I would ...

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He spoke loudly ____ everyone in the room could hear him.
questions.explanation: 'So that' + could expresses purpose: he spoke loudly in order that everyone could hear.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The police are investigating the accident to find out what ____.
questions.explanation: The accident is a finished past event, so the reported clause uses the simple past: what happened.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She has been working here ____ ten years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time (ten years); 'since' is used with a starting point.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ it is late, let's continue working.
questions.explanation: The sentence concedes that it is late, so the concession linker 'even though' fits.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The book ____ I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
questions.explanation: A thing (book) that is the object of 'borrowed' takes the relative pronoun 'which'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He promised ____ help me with my project.
questions.explanation: 'Promise' is followed by the to-infinitive: promised to help.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We must be quiet, ____ the baby is sleeping.
questions.explanation: The baby sleeping is the reason for being quiet, so the cause linker 'because' is used.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The more I think about it, ____ sense it makes.
questions.explanation: The double comparative pattern needs 'the more ... the more': the more sense it makes.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By next year, they ____ the new bridge.
questions.explanation: A project completed before a future point uses the future perfect: will have built.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She denied ____ the money.
questions.explanation: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund: denied taking the money.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: He was too tired ____ any more work.
questions.explanation: The 'too + adjective + to-infinitive' pattern is needed: too tired to do.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I look forward ____ from you soon.
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' uses a gerund after the preposition 'to': to hearing from you.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The examination is ____ difficult for most students.
questions.explanation: An adjective like 'difficult' is modified by 'quite'; 'very much' is used with verbs or past participles.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We ____ to leave early tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'be supposed to' + verb: we are supposed to leave early.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ____ the bad weather, the flight was not cancelled.
questions.explanation: Before a noun phrase we need the preposition 'despite'; 'although' needs a full clause.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: She is the girl ____ I mentioned in my letter.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of 'mentioned', referring to a person: whom.
